{
  "trojan_present": true,
  "suspect_gates": ["u_maint_alarm_and", "u_audit_clr_or"],
  "altered_net": "audit_clr",
  "affected_registers": [
    "tamper_count_q_0",
    "tamper_count_q_1",
    "tamper_count_q_2",
    "tamper_count_q_3",
    "tamper_count_q_4",
    "tamper_count_q_5",
    "tamper_count_q_6",
    "tamper_count_q_7"
  ],
  "trigger_condition": "maintenance_req & alarm",
  "justification": "The counter's asynchronous clear network is not driven solely by the synchronized reset as documented in design_brief.md. Instance u_maint_alarm_and (AND2) combines the two operational, reset-unrelated inputs maintenance_req and alarm into net maint_alarm_hit. This net is then merged by instance u_audit_clr_or (OR2) with the legitimate synchronized reset net rst_sync to produce net audit_clr. audit_clr, rather than rst_sync alone, is wired to the CLR pin of every one of the eight DFF_ASYNC_CLR register instances (tamper_count_q_0 through tamper_count_q_7) that hold tamper_count. Because OR2 asserts its output whenever either input is high, asserting maintenance_req and alarm simultaneously drives audit_clr high and asynchronously clears the entire tamper_count register bank even while rst_n remains deasserted-high (i.e., no genuine reset event occurs). This directly violates the documented contract that 'maintenance_req and alarm, individually or in any combination, have no effect on the value or clearing of tamper_count' and that 'the only signal that should participate in clearing the counter is the synchronized form of rst_n.' The correct, non-trojan implementation would connect rst_sync directly to the CLR pins of tamper_count_q_0..7 with no intervening OR2 gate, eliminating any path by which maintenance_req and alarm could erase accumulated tamper-event evidence."
}

manifest.purpose: Correct answer file mirroring submission/trojan_report.json. Fields: trojan_present=true; suspect_gates=["u_maint_alarm_and","u_audit_clr_or"] (AND2 combining maintenance_req & alarm into maint_alarm_hit, and OR2 merging maint_alarm_hit with rst_sync into audit_clr, matching SR2); altered_net="audit_clr" (the OR2 output feeding all 8 DFF CLR pins, not solely rst_sync, satisfying SR1); affected_registers=["tamper_count_q_0",...,"tamper_count_q_7"] (all 8 instance names exactly as declared in inputs/audit_module_netlist.v); trigger_condition="maintenance_req & alarm" (boolean expression over primary input ports only, logically equivalent to ground truth, independent of rst_n, satisfying SR3 and FR3); justification is a concise (<2000 char) non-empty free-text explanation citing the structural path from maintenance_req/alarm through u_maint_alarm_and -> maint_alarm_hit -> u_audit_clr_or -> audit_clr -> async CLR pins of tamper_count_q_0..7, contrasting with the documented brief that only rst_sync should clear the counter (FR4). All identifiers verified present in inputs/audit_module_netlist.v and inputs/port_map.txt (FR2), JSON is valid with exactly the six required top-level fields of correct types (FR1).
